To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fibrin/fibrinogens in lungs and respiratory tract secretions of horses are related to the presence of neutrophils, chronic small airway and chronic granulomatosis/bronchointerstitial pulmonary diseases, and to procoagulant and protease activities in respiratory tract secretions.

fibrin/fibrin(ogen) is found in the lungs of horses with chronic small airway or granulomatous disease, that the concentration of fibrin/fibrino(ge) in the lungs of these horses increases with the severity of the disease, and that fibrin/fibri(ogen) is present in respiratory secretions in proportion to the number of neutrophils present.
fibrin or fibriongen was detected in respiratory secretions and in lung specimens from horses with chronic small airway or granulomatous disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the presence and role of fibrin/fibrinogens in the pathogenesis of chronic pulmonary disease in the horse.
the role of fibrin and fibrinogen in the pathogenesis of chronic pulmonary disease in the horse.
the presence of soluble fibrin/fibrinoligomers in the lungs and respiratory secretory products of horses with chronic small airway, granulomatous, and bronchointerstital pneumonia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fibrinogen/fibrin is present in the lungs and respiratory secretory cells of horses with chronic lung disease.
the presence of SFD is associated with the presence of neutrophils and the degree of pulmonary disease.
the fibrin/fibrin(ogen) system may be involved in the pathogenesis of chronic pulmonary disease in horses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the concentration of SFD in respiratory secretions is positively correlated with the severity of chronic small airways disease.

fibrinogen is present in the lung and respiratory tract of the horse with chronic small airway and bronchointerstial disease and that the fibrinogen may be converted to fibrin by neutrophil proteases.
the concentration of fibrin/fibrinogens in the respiratory secretions and lungs of horses with chronic small airway, granulomatous, or bronchointerstial pneumonia is elevated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fibrin/fibrinolysis may be an important component of the pathogenesis of chronic small airways disease in horses.
the presence of fibrinous material in respiratory secretions and lungs of horses with chronic small airway and granulomatous diseases may indicate the presence of inflammation.

the presence of fibrino(fibrin)ogen and fibrin(ogen) in respiratory secretions of the horse is associated with the presence of fibrinous exudate within the airways of horses with chronic bronchointertitial pneumonia.
